facts.title: Title
feature.action_menu.a1: Yes: Settings → Behaviour → Right-click → Opens the action menu. Both apps follow it; in the desktop app Ctrl+right-click then marks.
feature.action_menu.a2: It does not fit what is under the cursor: Rename, Edit and Properties need one entry, and read-only places list nothing that changes files. Every action is still in Commands ({menu}).
feature.action_menu.a3: Each hint shows three times, then makes room for the next. Settings → Behaviour → Show the hints again, or coxswain --hints reset, brings them all back.
feature.action_menu.q1: Can right-click open the menu instead of marking?
feature.action_menu.q2: Why is an action I expected missing from the menu?
feature.action_menu.q3: Why did a hint disappear for good?
feature.action_menu.title: The action menu and hints
feature.action_menu.what: A menu of what fits the file or folder under the cursor, each with its key; the status line shows hints.
feature.archive_passwords.a1: No. A password lives in the running app's memory and is gone when you close it. It is never written to disk.
feature.archive_passwords.a2: In a zip only the contents of each file are locked, not the names or sizes. To hide the names too, pack into a 7z with Hide the file names too.
feature.archive_passwords.a3: Yes, with the password, in any program that reads AES zips (7-Zip, WinZip, Keka). Windows Explorer's built-in zip support has long not read them.
feature.archive_passwords.q1: Does Coxswain save my archive passwords?
feature.archive_passwords.q2: Why could I see the names in a locked zip without a password?
feature.archive_passwords.q3: Can others open the zip I locked?
feature.archive_passwords.title: Archive passwords
feature.archive_passwords.what: A locked zip or 7z asks for its password when needed and keeps it in memory; {pack} can lock a new one.
feature.archives.a1: Press {open} on the zip, go to the file and press {copy}. It is copied to the other panel's folder; nothing else is unpacked.
feature.archives.a2: Open the archive with {open} in one panel. In the other panel, mark the files and press {copy}. They are added to the folder of the archive you have open.
feature.archives.a3: The archive is written anew into a .coxswain-tmp file next to it and only then renamed over the old one. If something fails, the new file is removed.
feature.archives.q1: How do I get one file out of a zip without unpacking all of it?
feature.archives.q2: How do I add files to an existing archive?
feature.archives.q3: Is it safe to change an archive? What if the power goes off?
feature.archives.title: Archives as folders
feature.archives.what: A zip, tar or 7z opens like a folder with {open}; the usual file keys copy out of it, into it and between archives.
feature.ask.a1: With the built-in chat model, nothing. With a server's, the question, the turns before it and ten passages with their paths, to the chat model on that server. Nothing to anyone else.
feature.ask.a2: The model answers from the sources only. Ask with other words, or check with {search_text} that the file is read: folders not read, Names only folders and files waiting for vectors are not searched.
feature.ask.a3: The server loads the model into memory on the first question, which can take half a minute. Waiting for … to answer shows until the first word; Esc stops the wait.
feature.ask.q2: Why does it say the sources do not hold the answer?
feature.ask.q3: The first answer takes long. Why?
feature.ask.title: Ask
feature.ask.what: Answers a question from the passages of your files closest to it, citing them as [1], [2] with the sources listed.
feature.ask_code.a1: It reads it as code: whole functions and classes with their lines and indentation, each named after its item, in any language. The answer is still the chat model's: a larger model with more room sees more.
feature.ask_code.a2: Words such as architecture, framework, library or dependencies make it a question about the whole project: Ask reads its overview first, with a map of each file, its public items and what the project files say it uses.
feature.ask_code.a3: Files are now cut into passages another way, code at its items: every vector is made again once and code is read again with its indentation. Word search works meanwhile.
feature.ask_code.q2: Why does a question about libraries get the README and a list of files?
feature.ask_code.q3: Why is search by meaning re-reading my files?
feature.ask_code.title: Ask about code
feature.ask_code.what: Ask reads code as code: whole functions with their lines, named after their item, and a map of the project for questions about it as a whole.
feature.ask_builtin.a1: The largest the Mac has the memory for: Qwen3 14B with 32 GB or more, Qwen3 4B Instruct with 16 GB, else Qwen3 1.7B, which is also the one for a processor. Settings lists only the models that fit.
feature.ask_builtin.a2: It runs on the processor there, which reads the prompt about as fast as it writes the answer. When a server such as Ollama runs a model on your graphics card, Settings → Ask says so in red with a Use button, and Find shows the same line under the Ask row.
feature.ask_builtin.a3: The memory frees itself five minutes after the last answer, or at once with Unload now under Settings → Finding files → Built-in models. Delete there frees the disk; the terminal app also has coxswain --models delete.
feature.ask_builtin.q2: Why is it so slow on my PC?
feature.ask_builtin.q3: How do I free the memory or the disk?
feature.ask_builtin.title: Ask without a server
feature.ask_builtin.what: A built-in Qwen3 chat model, downloaded once, answers Ask on this machine: on a Mac's GPU, else the processor.
feature.batch_rename.a1: A name in the list is red (a conflict), or no name changes. Read the reason next to the red one.
feature.batch_rename.a2: The order of the list, which is the folder's current sort order. Sort first to number by name, extension, date or size.
feature.batch_rename.a3: With Include extension unticked, only the part before the last dot is matched and the extension is kept. Tick it to change the whole name.
feature.batch_rename.q1: Why is the Rename button greyed out?
feature.batch_rename.q2: In which order does the counter count?
feature.batch_rename.q3: Why was the extension not changed?
feature.batch_rename.title: Batch rename
feature.batch_rename.what: In the desktop app, {batch_rename} renames many files at once with a regular expression and a counter, shown first.
feature.battery.a1: No. Names, text and meaning are searched as usual. Only reading new and changed files, hashing them and making vectors wait.
feature.battery.a2: It reports a battery; a UPS can look like one. Press Read now in Settings → Finding files, or check what /sys/class/power_supply lists.
feature.battery.a3: Until the backlog is done. After that, new files wait for the mains again.
feature.battery.q1: Does search stop working on battery?
feature.battery.q2: My desktop PC says it is paused for battery.
feature.battery.q3: I pressed Read now on battery. Does it stay on?
feature.battery.title: Pause on battery
feature.battery.what: On battery the helper stops reading files and making vectors until the mains is back; searching goes on.
feature.bills_of_materials.a1: Coxswain uses them only to read the text of old encrypted PDFs for search, never to protect anything new. The CBOM records the purpose with each algorithm.
feature.bills_of_materials.a2: There are two products: the terminal app has no web frontend, and the desktop app has crates the terminal app lacks. Each SBOM says what that download holds.
feature.bills_of_materials.a3: In THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md, next to LICENSE: in the terminal app's archive, in the desktop app's install folder, and on every release's Assets list.
feature.bills_of_materials.q1: Why are RC4 and MD5 in the CBOM, rated broken?
feature.bills_of_materials.q2: Why are there two SBOMs and not one?
feature.bills_of_materials.q3: Where are the licences of the apps I installed?
feature.bills_of_materials.title: Licences and bills of materials
feature.bills_of_materials.what: Every release carries an SBOM per app, a CBOM of its cryptography, and the licence text of every component.
feature.cbom.a1: The rating needs a parameter the BOM does not give: RSA-1024 is broken, RSA-2048 acceptable, so it is never guessed. The details box says what is missing.
feature.cbom.a2: A folder shows the worst rating beneath it, so one DSA key turns it red. Put the cursor on it: the details box names the asset responsible.
feature.cbom.a3: In the viewer, s opens the BOM in your pager. To make {view} always open the pager, set bom_viewer = false, or untick it in Settings → Behaviour.
feature.cbom.q1: Why is an RSA key "Unknown", when RSA is fine?
feature.cbom.q2: Why is a whole folder red when almost everything in it is green?
feature.cbom.q3: How do I get the old {view} back in the terminal app?
feature.cbom.title: Cryptography bills of materials
feature.cbom.what: Shows a CycloneDX CBOM as a rated tree or sunburst: which cryptography is weak, where it is, what changed.
feature.change_keys.a1: In config.toml, under [keys]. Settings → Keys → Open config.toml in the desktop app, or the row Change keys in config.toml in the terminal app, opens it there. Restart the app afterwards.
feature.change_keys.a2: List both, as search = ["Alt+F7", "Ctrl+F", "Ctrl+P"]. Listing an action replaces all of its defaults.
feature.change_keys.a3: A key name it does not know, such as Ctlr+P. The terminal app stops with unknown key; the desktop app starts with the defaults. {help} lists every action with its keys.
feature.change_keys.q1: Where do I change a key?
feature.change_keys.q2: How do I keep the default key and add my own?
feature.change_keys.q3: I bound a key and the app will not start. What is wrong?
feature.change_keys.title: Changing keys
feature.change_keys.what: The [keys] table in config.toml gives any action other keys, more keys, or none, the same in both apps.
feature.chromeos.a1: Run dpkg --print-architecture in the Linux terminal: amd64 takes the _amd64.deb, arm64 the _arm64.deb.
feature.chromeos.a2: Linux sees only Linux files until a folder is shared. In the Files app, right-click Downloads and choose Share with Linux; it is then at /mnt/chromeos/MyFiles/Downloads.
feature.chromeos.a3: No. Linux on ChromeOS has no GPU for computing; the built-in model runs on the processor.
feature.chromeos.q2: Why does Coxswain not see my Downloads folder?
feature.chromeos.q3: Does search by meaning use the Chromebook's graphics?
feature.chromeos.title: ChromeOS
feature.chromeos.what: Runs both apps in a Chromebook's Linux development environment, with the Linux .deb for its processor.
feature.clipboard.a1: There is no common way to mark a cut on the clipboard, so another program sees a copy. Paste in Coxswain to move, or delete the originals afterwards.
feature.clipboard.a2: A file of that name was already in the folder. Paste keeps both and numbers the new one. Use {copy} if you would rather get an error.
feature.clipboard.a3: No. A terminal has no access to the system's file clipboard, and Ctrl+C belongs to the terminal. Use {copy} and {move} there.
feature.clipboard.q1: I cut files in Coxswain and pasted them in my other file manager; they were copied.
feature.clipboard.q2: Why did the pasted file get (2) in its name?
feature.clipboard.q3: Does the terminal app have it?
feature.clipboard.title: Clipboard
feature.clipboard.what: In the desktop app, {clip_copy} and {clip_cut} put files on the system clipboard and {paste} pastes them.
feature.cloud_files.a1: No. A file that is only online is found by name and left in the cloud: not read, hashed, thumbnailed or previewed until you open that one file yourself.
feature.cloud_files.a2: Make the folder available offline in Dropbox; Coxswain reads the files once they are on disk. Or press Read its files next to Dropbox under Settings → Finding files → Details → What is read.
feature.cloud_files.a3: In the panels: a cloud glyph after the name. Find shows no glyph; the panel does once you go to the file.
feature.cloud_files.q2: How do I search inside my Dropbox files?
feature.cloud_files.q3: Can I see which files are online-only?
feature.cloud_files.title: Cloud files
feature.cloud_files.what: Online-only files in OneDrive, Dropbox, Google Drive, Proton Drive and iCloud are found by name, never downloaded.
feature.command_line.a1: In the terminal app, yes: the panels step aside and the program has the terminal. In the desktop app, no: a command gets no input and its output is collected, so sudo cannot ask for your password.
feature.command_line.a2: Press {toggle_panels}: the panels hide and the terminal shows what the command printed. Any key brings the panels back.
feature.command_line.a3: The terminal app uses your $SHELL; the desktop app always uses sh. Write the line for sh, or call your shell yourself: fish -c '…'.
feature.command_line.q1: Can I run vim, less, ssh or sudo from the command line?
feature.command_line.q2: The output flashed by in the terminal app. Where is it?
feature.command_line.q3: My fish (or zsh) syntax works in the terminal app but not in the desktop app.
feature.command_line.title: Command line
feature.command_line.what: Type a shell command under the panels and press Enter to run it in the active panel's folder.
feature.command_line_flags.a1: coxswain --version prints it. In the desktop app, the title of Help ({help}) and the window title show it.
feature.command_line_flags.a2: The desktop app takes arguments it does not know as folders. Use coxswain --help.
feature.command_line_flags.a3: A flag is looked at only as the first argument. In coxswain ~/src --paths, --paths is taken as the right panel's folder. Put the flag first.
feature.command_line_flags.q1: How do I find out which version I have?
feature.command_line_flags.q3: Why is a flag after a folder ignored?
feature.command_line_flags.title: Command-line flags
feature.command_line_flags.what: Starts either app in given folders or at a Settings area, prints paths and defaults, sets up search.
feature.command_list.a1: {menu} opens the searchable list Commands instead; it reaches every action. For the actions that fit the file under the cursor, press {action_menu}.
feature.command_list.a2: Find it in Commands ({menu}): Folder sizes and Columns and folder sizes have no key by default. Or give it one in config.toml.
feature.command_list.a3: {help} shows its path at the bottom. coxswain --config-path prints it.
feature.command_list.q2: How do I run an action that has no key?
feature.command_list.q3: How do I find the config file?
feature.command_list.title: Commands and Help
feature.command_list.what: {menu} lists every action with its key, filtered as you type; {help} shows your keys by group.
feature.configuration.a1: The terminal app reads it when it starts: quit with {quit} and start again. The desktop app reads it at start and after a change in Settings: restart it.
feature.configuration.a2: Only mistakes that make the file unreadable are refused. A misspelt setting name is ignored and the default stays; compare with coxswain --dump-config.
feature.configuration.a3: No. Settings and the --meaning flags change only the one value, in place, and keep your comments, order and blank lines.
feature.configuration.q1: I edited config.toml and nothing changed.
feature.configuration.q2: I misspelt a key and Coxswain said nothing.
feature.configuration.q3: Will Settings mess up my comments?
feature.configuration.title: Configuration file
feature.configuration.what: Both apps read one config.toml; set only what you change. Every key, its default and its Settings item.
feature.containers.a1: Yes. The container has no network, sees the project read-only, writes only to a fresh cache folder, and LaTeX runs without -shell-escape.
feature.containers.a2: Its image is not pulled yet, and a 5 GB download never starts without a click. Press Build PDF, or Pull it in Settings → Previews first.
feature.containers.a3: No. Pull in Settings fetches the newest version of the tag when you press it. Nothing is updated or removed by itself.
feature.containers.q1: Is it safe to build someone else's LaTeX document in a container?
feature.containers.q2: The LaTeX container never starts by itself.
feature.containers.title: Containers for previews
feature.containers.what: Runs a missing preview tool from a podman or docker image, with no network and your files read-only.
feature.copy.a1: Coxswain never overwrites. Delete the old one first ({delete}), or copy under another name by typing it into the target.
feature.copy.a2: The cause line leaves the path out to stay short. Unfold Details in the desktop app, or read below Details: in the terminal app.
feature.copy.a3: Type the new name, or a path ending in it, into the target. When that path does not exist, the file is copied under that name.
feature.copy.q1: How do I overwrite a file that exists?
feature.copy.q2: The error says only Permission denied. Which file?
feature.copy.q3: How do I copy a file and give the copy a new name?
feature.copy.title: Copy
feature.copy.what: {copy} copies the marked files, or the one under the cursor, to the other panel's folder or a path you type.
feature.default_keys.a1: In config.toml, under keys, list the action with its new keys. Listing an action replaces its default keys; an empty list unbinds it.
feature.default_keys.a2: A key it cannot read makes the config invalid: the terminal app refuses to start and names it, the desktop app starts with every default. Fix the name and restart.
feature.default_keys.a3: Both apps read the same keys, and Norton Commander's keys are Ctrl keys. Cmd-click still marks, as in other Mac apps.
feature.default_keys.q1: How do I change a key?
feature.default_keys.q2: I bound a key and now the desktop app ignores my whole config. Why?
feature.default_keys.q3: Why are the shortcuts Ctrl on a Mac, not Cmd?
feature.default_keys.title: Every default key
feature.default_keys.what: Every key both apps have out of the box, with its name in Commands and its config name.
feature.delete.a1: Untick Settings → Behaviour → Ask before deleting. Be careful: {delete_forever} then deletes for good without a question.
feature.delete.a2: Not every file system has a bin the system can use. The error names the file. Use {delete_forever} to delete it for good, after checking.
feature.delete.a3: Not from Coxswain, and {undo} does not either. It is removed as rm would remove it. Only backups or recovery tools can help.
feature.delete.q1: How do I stop Coxswain asking every time?
feature.delete.q2: Moving to the bin fails on a network share or a USB stick.
feature.delete.q3: Can I get back a file I deleted with {delete_forever}?
feature.delete.title: Delete
feature.delete.what: {delete} moves the marked files to the system's bin; {delete_forever} deletes them for good. Both ask first.
feature.disk_use.a1: Everything in the list but your models comes back by itself. Clear everything that can be built again takes the search store, the name index, previews and copies; the store is then read again at half speed.
feature.disk_use.a2: No. Only the images named in [preview] images and a Tectonic cache Coxswain made itself are listed, and each goes only on its own click, after the exact list is shown.
feature.disk_use.a3: {disk_use} in the command list ({menu}), Settings ({settings}) → Privacy and updates → Disk use, or coxswain --disk in a terminal.
feature.disk_use.q1: What can I clear without losing anything?
feature.disk_use.q2: Will it delete container images or caches that are mine?
feature.disk_use.title: Disk use
feature.disk_use.what: Shows every place Coxswain keeps things, and what it caused outside its folder, with sizes and what clearing costs, and clears them.
feature.drag_and_drop.a1: No: a drop always goes to the folder the pane shows. Open the folder first.
feature.drag_and_drop.a2: Yes. Open the archive in a pane and drop on it; Copy here (C) adds the files, Move here (M) adds them and deletes the originals.
feature.drag_and_drop.a3: Not reliably: a file inside an archive is not on disk. Copy it out first with {copy}, then drag it.
feature.drag_and_drop.q1: Can I drop onto a folder inside the pane?
feature.drag_and_drop.q2: Can I drop files into an archive?
feature.drag_and_drop.q3: Can I drag files out of an archive to another program?
feature.drag_and_drop.title: Drag and drop
feature.drag_and_drop.what: In the desktop app, drag files out to other applications, between panes, and in; a drop asks copy or move.
feature.duplicates.a1: They are not byte for byte the same, or smaller than Ignore files under, or one is in a hidden folder with Include hidden files off. Or they are hard links to one file.
feature.duplicates.a2: They go to the bin, not away for good, and at least one copy of each group always stays. Check with Show first if the folder matters.
feature.duplicates.a3: Yes: plug it in and it appears under Look in. Tick both and scan, then Mark all but the one under your home folder marks the copies on the backup.
feature.duplicates.q1: Why are two identical photos not found?
feature.duplicates.q2: Is it safe to move the marked copies?
feature.duplicates.q3: Can I compare my home folder with a USB backup disk?
feature.duplicates.title: Finding duplicates
feature.duplicates.what: In the desktop app, {duplicates} finds duplicate files and folders by content and moves extra copies to the bin.
feature.favourites.a1: The folder is already in that group, or + added the folder you are in, not the one under the cursor. Go into the folder first.
feature.favourites.a2: No. The folders are untouched, only the group is gone. Make the group again and add the folders back.
feature.favourites.a3: Click the ⋯ at the right of the group's header, or right-click the header: the menu has Add current folder, Rename group and Delete group.
feature.favourites.q1: I clicked + and nothing was added. Why?
feature.favourites.q2: Deleting a group asks nothing. Can I undo it?
feature.favourites.q3: How do I rename or delete a group?
feature.favourites.title: Favourites
feature.favourites.what: Folders you go to often, in named groups in the desktop app's sidebar, one click away.
feature.features.a1: Press {help} and switch to Features (the tab in the desktop app, Tab in the terminal app), then type a word: the features and questions that hold it stay.
feature.features.a2: It opens the feature's page on GitHub in your browser, and only when you press it. Nothing else in Features reaches the network.
feature.features.a3: It opens Features at the feature that dialog belongs to: in Copy, the copy questions; in Settings, those about Settings.
feature.features.q1: How do I find out what a key or a feature does?
feature.features.q3: What does {help} do inside a dialog?
feature.features.title: Features and questions
feature.features.what: {help}, then Features: every feature with its keys and the questions people ask, filtered as you type.
feature.find_file.a1: Press {search} again inside Find, or click In <folder> in the desktop app. Every group, and Ask, then keeps to the active panel's folder and below; press it again for everywhere.
feature.find_file.a2: It follows what you typed. One or two words put Names first; three words or a question put In files and About this first. Name syntax shows names only.
feature.find_file.a3: One word is almost always a name. Type a second word, end with ?, or press Ctrl+Enter (desktop app) or Alt+Enter (terminal app) to ask anyway.
feature.find_file.q1: How do I search only this folder?
feature.find_file.q2: Why does the order of the groups change?
feature.find_file.q3: Why is there no Ask row for one word?
feature.find_file.title: Find
feature.find_file.what: One field for names, words inside files, files about something, git history and questions to Ask.
feature.first_run.a1: Yes. Press {help}, then Show the guide again in the desktop app or G in the terminal app; or use Settings → Overview.
feature.first_run.a2: No. Only the choices you made on the steps you saw are saved.
feature.first_run.a3: Your terminal's font has no Nerd Font symbols. Choose Plain characters in step 3, or install a Nerd Font and pick it in your terminal's settings.
feature.first_run.q1: I skipped the guide. Can I get it back?
feature.first_run.q3: Why are the icons boxes in the terminal app?
feature.first_run.title: First-run guide
feature.first_run.what: A four-step guide on the first start: the panels and their keys, how far Find looks, looks and privacy.
feature.folder_sizes.a1: It is still being measured, you left the folder, measuring is off (Settings → Behaviour → Measure folder sizes), or it is /proc, /sys, /dev or /run.
feature.folder_sizes.a2: A change made outside Coxswain deep in a folder not on screen goes unnoticed for up to five minutes. Pick Folder sizes in Commands ({menu}) to measure again now.
feature.folder_sizes.a3: du counts the disk blocks a file takes; Coxswain counts the bytes in it. Sparse files, compression and many small files make the two differ.
feature.folder_sizes.q1: Why is a folder's size not shown?
feature.folder_sizes.q2: A size is out of date. Why?
feature.folder_sizes.q3: Why does Coxswain's size differ from du?
feature.folder_sizes.title: Folder sizes
feature.folder_sizes.what: Folders show their size in the Size column, measured in the background, in both apps.
feature.git.a1: The folder is not inside a git work tree, or git is not on your PATH. Inside an archive there is no git line either.
feature.git.a2: Both apps watch the repository's .git and follow within a moment. Where the file system sends no change events (some network shares, WSL mounts), press {refresh}.
feature.git.a3: No. It switches branches and makes new ones when you ask, and otherwise only reads. Put the commands you want in the user menu ({user_menu}) or a script.
feature.git.q1: Why is there no git line?
feature.git.q2: Why did the git line not change after I committed?
feature.git.title: Git in the panels
feature.git.what: In a repository: the branch, ahead and behind, change counts, a glyph per file and its last commit.
feature.git_branches.a1: {branches}, the cursor on the branch, {switch_branch}, then Enter. The status line says Switched to branch '…' and the git line shows the new branch.
feature.git_branches.a2: A file you changed differs between the two branches, so git refuses, and so does Coxswain. Commit or stash your change first, then switch again.
feature.git_branches.a3: {open} on it in the list of branches: its files at its last commit, read-only. {copy} copies one out.
feature.git_branches.q1: How do I switch to another branch?
feature.git_branches.q2: Why did the switch say my changes would be overwritten?
feature.git_branches.q3: How do I look at another branch's files without switching?
feature.git_branches.title: Git branches and worktrees
feature.git_branches.what: Lists branches and worktrees as folders: browse a branch's files, switch to it or make a new one.
feature.git_history.a1: {history} on the file, {open} on the commit you want, then {copy} on the file to copy it to the other panel. Copying never overwrites.
feature.git_history.a2: In the desktop app, put the cursor on the file inside the commit and pick Diff at the top of the preview pane. For the whole commit, use the user menu's git log ({user_menu}, l).
feature.git_history.a3: A list has at most 2000, and git gets four seconds for it. Use git log on the command line for the full history.
feature.git_history.q1: How do I get back an old version of a file?
feature.git_history.q2: How do I see what a commit changed?
feature.git_history.q3: Why do I not see all commits?
feature.git_history.title: Git history as folders
feature.git_history.what: Opens a file's or folder's commits like an archive: browse, preview and copy out old versions.
feature.glyphs_and_fonts.a1: No Nerd Font is installed (desktop app: none in Icon font), or the terminal's font is not one. Install one, such as Symbols Nerd Font Mono, or choose Plain characters (ASCII).
feature.glyphs_and_fonts.a2: The theme brings its own: the Windows and Mac themes their era's fonts, Cyber and NC the monospaced font. Font applies to Dark, Light, Nord and Tokyo Night.
feature.glyphs_and_fonts.a3: Text size in Settings → Looks, up to 28. The rows, lists and dialogs grow with it. The terminal app uses the terminal's own font and size.
feature.glyphs_and_fonts.q2: Why is the font I picked not used?
feature.glyphs_and_fonts.q3: How do I make everything bigger?
feature.glyphs_and_fonts.title: Glyphs and fonts
feature.glyphs_and_fonts.what: Nerd Font or plain-character glyphs for files and git states, and in the desktop app the fonts and text size.
feature.helper.a1: Yes, the helper, for ten minutes, so the next window searches at once. Then it exits. With Start with my session it stays for good.
feature.helper.a2: Close every Coxswain window and wait ten minutes. With Start with my session on, untick it or run coxswain --index-service off. Do not kill it by name: an open app would start another.
feature.helper.a3: So the first pass over your files, and the vectors for search by meaning, are done while no window is open. Otherwise reading happens only while an app runs and ten minutes after.
feature.helper.q1: Is Coxswain running in the background after I close it?
feature.helper.q2: How do I stop the helper?
feature.helper.q3: Why start it with my session?
feature.helper.title: The search helper
feature.helper.what: One background process holds the index for every window and terminal app; it can start with your session.
feature.html.a1: Its content comes from JavaScript, or its styles from the web, and neither reaches the preview. Press {open} for your browser, or Source to read the HTML.
feature.html.a2: No. Tracking pixels, web fonts and scripts are all blocked, so nothing leaves your machine when the preview shows a page.
feature.html.a3: The preview is for looking. Open the page with {open} to follow its links in your browser.
feature.html.q1: Why does the page look broken or empty?
feature.html.q2: Can a downloaded page find out that I looked at it?
feature.html.q3: Can I click links in the preview?
feature.html.title: HTML pages, sandboxed
feature.html.what: Shows HTML files as a browser would, with their styles and pictures, but runs no script and fetches nothing.
feature.languages.a1: The terminal app reads the language when it starts. Quit it ({quit}) and start it again.
feature.languages.a2: US English, and English without a region, get Canadian English: British spelling, North American words. Pick English (United Kingdom) in Settings for bin.
feature.languages.a3: Settings → Looks → Language → Automatic, or language = "auto" in config.toml (or delete the line).
feature.languages.q1: I changed the language in Settings and the terminal app still speaks the old one.
feature.languages.q2: My system is in US English. Why does Coxswain say colour but trash?
feature.languages.q3: How do I go back to following the system?
feature.languages.title: Languages
feature.languages.what: Both apps speak 29 languages from one setting; by default Coxswain follows your system's language.
feature.latex.a1: A file without \documentclass builds the document that includes it, as a LaTeX editor would: the one its % !TEX root line names, or one nearby that names it.
feature.latex.a2: latexmk could not make the PDF (here a missing package), so the next ready engine was tried and succeeded. Install the package, or pick tectonic's button.
feature.latex.a3: It needs -shell-escape, which lets a document run programs on your machine. Coxswain never passes it, so no document can run a command.
feature.latex.q1: A chapter file shows the whole book. Why?
feature.latex.q2: It says "Built with tectonic: latexmk stopped". What happened?
feature.latex.title: LaTeX projects
feature.latex.what: Shows the PDF of a LaTeX document from any of its .tex files, built with the right engine when sources change.
feature.linux_arm.a1: No. There is no armhf build. A Pi 3 or newer can run the 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS instead; uname -m must say aarch64.
feature.linux_arm.a2: Install FUSE 2: sudo apt install libfuse2 (libfuse2t64 on Ubuntu 24.04 and newer), or run it with --appimage-extract-and-run. The .deb needs neither.
feature.linux_arm.a3: The built-in model runs on the Pi's processor. Use a model server on another computer, or let it run overnight; words inside files need no model.
feature.linux_arm.q1: Does it run on the 32-bit Raspberry Pi OS?
feature.linux_arm.q2: The AppImage does not start and mentions FUSE. What now?
feature.linux_arm.q3: Why is search by meaning so slow on my Pi?
feature.linux_arm.title: Linux on ARM
feature.linux_arm.what: Native builds of both apps for 64-bit ARM Linux: Raspberry Pi, Asahi Linux, ARM laptops and servers.
feature.looks.a1: The look brings its era's font and puts it over yours. Font applies to the modern look (Dark, Light, Nord, Tokyo Night); Monospaced font is yours in every look.
feature.looks.a2: Coxswain does not ship fonts. Install a Chicago-like font (ChicagoFLF is free) and the look picks it up at the next start.
feature.looks.a3: No. A look draws its chrome from the theme's colours. Pick Windows 11 (dark) or macOS (dark) for a dark system.
feature.looks.q1: Why is my font setting not used in Windows 95?
feature.looks.q2: Why does Mac System 7 not have the Chicago font on Linux?
feature.looks.q3: Do the looks follow my system's own theme or accent colour?
feature.looks.title: Looks
feature.looks.what: In the desktop app, each theme brings its era's shapes: corners, bevels, title bars, buttons and the interface font.
feature.macos.a1: To find your files there by name and by their text. Answer Don't Allow and those folders are simply not searched; everything else works.
feature.macos.a2: The builds are ad-hoc signed, so each version looks like a new app to macOS. Your files are not read any differently; answer as before.
feature.macos.a3: No. The built-in model runs on the Mac's GPU through Metal, and so can the built-in chat model for Ask.
feature.macos.q1: Why does Coxswain want my Desktop, Documents and Downloads?
feature.macos.q2: After an update macOS asked about my folders again. Why?
feature.macos.q3: Do I need Ollama for search by meaning on a Mac?
feature.macos.title: macOS
feature.macos.what: What is particular to a Mac: folder prompts, what is never read, the helper at login, meaning on the GPU.
feature.marking.a1: Groups mark files only, as in Norton Commander. Mark folders one by one with {mark} or a right-click.
feature.marking.a2: {mark_all} marks every file and folder. For files only, press {invert_marks} with nothing marked, or {mark_group} and Enter with the * it offers.
feature.marking.a3: You left the folder, or an operation finished: both clear the marks, as in NC. Switching tabs in the desktop app keeps each tab's marks.
feature.marking.q1: Why did {mark_group} not mark any folders?
feature.marking.q2: How do I mark every file?
feature.marking.title: Marking files
feature.marking.what: Mark files one by one, by pattern or all at once, then copy, move, delete or tag them together.
feature.meaning.a1: It needs a 465 MB model that Coxswain does not ship, and processor time to read your files. Turn it on with the level Names, text and meaning in Settings → Finding files, or coxswain --meaning on.
feature.meaning.a2: The vectors are made in the background, a few files at a time, and wait on battery. Settings shows how many are done; on a laptop's processor a large home folder takes hours.
feature.meaning.a3: Both apps say why in red. No vectors: … is the server or the model, such as Ollama not running or the model not pulled. Reading stopped: … means a scan failed before the vectors' turn.
feature.meaning.q1: Why is search by meaning off?
feature.meaning.q2: Why does it find nothing yet?
feature.meaning.title: Search by meaning
feature.meaning.what: Finds files about what you type, whatever words they use and in any language, with a model on your machine.
feature.models.a1: In the models folder of the cache folder (coxswain --paths shows it). Settings → Finding files → Built-in models lists each with its folder and Show in panel; the terminal app also has coxswain --models.
feature.models.a2: Delete on a model, or Delete all not in use, which takes unfinished downloads and older versions too. In the terminal app: Delete on its row in Settings, or coxswain --models delete unused.
feature.models.a3: You are asked first. Ask or search by meaning then takes the recommended choice, a server's model on the graphics card when one answers, and the line says which.
feature.models.q1: Where are the built-in models kept?
feature.models.q2: How do I free the disk space?
feature.models.q3: What happens when I delete the model in use?
feature.models.title: Built-in models
feature.models.what: Lists the models Coxswain downloaded, with their size, folder, whether they are in use and loaded, and frees their memory or their disk space.
feature.mouse.a1: That is Norton Commander's way. Set Settings → Behaviour → Right-click to Opens the action menu; the menu is also on {action_menu} and, in the desktop app, Ctrl+right-click.
feature.mouse.a2: In the desktop app's details view, click the first entry, then Shift-click the last. Elsewhere, right-click or Ctrl-click each one.
feature.mouse.a3: The terminal passes the mouse on only when it supports mouse reporting and has it on. With it on, hold Shift to select text.
feature.mouse.q1: Why does right-click mark instead of opening a menu?
feature.mouse.q2: How do I mark a range with the mouse?
feature.mouse.q3: Mouse clicks in the terminal app select text instead. Why?
feature.mouse.title: The mouse
feature.mouse.what: Click to move, double-click to open, right-click to mark; the desktop app adds dragging and resizing.
feature.move_and_rename.a1: Something of that name is already in the target folder, and Coxswain never writes over it. Rename one of them first, or move the other one out of the way.
feature.move_and_rename.a2: No. A move into an archive adds the files to it and then deletes the originals for good. Copy with {copy} if you want to keep them.
feature.move_and_rename.a3: Yes: {undo}, in both apps, right after it or later in the same run, while nothing has changed the file since.
feature.move_and_rename.q1: Why did my move fail with exists?
feature.move_and_rename.q2: I moved files into a zip. Are the originals in the bin?
feature.move_and_rename.q3: Can I undo a move or rename?
feature.move_and_rename.title: Move and rename
feature.move_and_rename.what: {move} moves the marked files to another folder, or renames one when you type a new name; {rename} renames in place.
feature.moving.a1: That is Norton Commander's way. Rebind them to the parent folder and open actions if you prefer; in the desktop app's columns view they already walk the tree.
feature.moving.a2: Yes. The desktop app reads a changed folder again within a quarter of a second; the terminal app watches its two panels' folders and their .git. {refresh} reads them again by hand.
feature.moving.a3: The command line has text, and while it does, Backspace edits it. Press Esc to clear the command line.
feature.moving.q1: Why do Left and Right page instead of moving into folders?
feature.moving.q2: Do the panels follow changes on disk?
feature.moving.q3: Backspace deletes a character instead of going up. Why?
feature.moving.title: Moving around
feature.moving.what: Move in a panel, open with {open}, go up with {parent}, and type a path to jump to any folder.
feature.name_syntax.a1: Wildcards match the whole name. Use .rs (a plain substring) or *.rs* instead.
feature.name_syntax.a2: Put a / in a term: projects/ budget finds names with budget under a folder whose path has projects/. Or press {search} inside Find to search the panel's folder.
feature.name_syntax.a3: No. A query with name syntax shows names only. In files takes plain words; !, |, ext: and quotes mean nothing there.
feature.name_syntax.q2: How do I find something under a certain folder?
feature.name_syntax.q3: Does the syntax work for the words in files?
feature.name_syntax.title: Name syntax
feature.name_syntax.what: Everything-style terms for names: !, |, wildcards, ext:, file:, folder:, case:, quotes and path terms.
feature.names.a1: The watcher reports it within a second. On Linux, with more folders than fs.inotify.max_user_watches allows, the rest are caught only by the hourly rebuild: raise the limit or wait.
feature.names.a2: Every name is indexed, hidden ones too. Leave them out of one search with !node_modules/, or out of the index under Settings → Finding files → Details → Never indexed.
feature.names.a3: There is no saved index yet, so hits come in as the disk is walked: seconds to a minute. From the second start on, the saved index answers at once.
feature.names.q1: Why does a file I just made not show up?
feature.names.q2: Why do I see files from .cache and node_modules?
feature.names.q3: Why does the first search say building index?
feature.names.title: Names everywhere
feature.names.what: Every file and folder on the machine is in a name index, found by name in milliseconds, with nothing to set up.
feature.new_folder.a1: Yes: type the whole path, photos/2026/summer. Every folder on the way that is missing is made.
feature.new_folder.a2: Not with a key of its own. Use the command line (touch notes.txt on Linux and macOS), or a user-menu entry.
feature.new_folder.a3: Yes. Open the zip with {open}, press {new_folder} and type the name. The zip gets a folder entry, so the folder stays even while it is empty.
feature.new_folder.q1: Can I make several nested folders at once?
feature.new_folder.q2: Can I make a new, empty file?
feature.new_folder.q3: Can I make a folder inside a zip?
feature.new_folder.title: New folder
feature.new_folder.what: {new_folder} makes a new folder in the active panel's folder, or a whole path of folders at once.
feature.notes.a1: No, when you leave the field: Esc, a click elsewhere, or moving the focus. Press Esc before you close the window.
feature.notes.a2: The folder you are in: the label says Notes for this folder. Files have no notes of their own; use a colour tag.
feature.notes.a3: A note belongs to a path, so it stays at the old path. Move the folder back, or copy the text into the note at the new place.
feature.notes.q1: Is my note saved while I type?
feature.notes.q2: I pressed {notes} on a file. Whose note is it?
feature.notes.q3: Where did my note go after I moved the folder?
feature.notes.title: Folder notes
feature.notes.what: Free text kept for a folder, shown at the bottom of the preview pane, in the desktop app.
feature.notices.a1: The tips you have not dismissed or acted on, plus the versions you have not read about. Click it: What's new opens and the number drops to the tips left.
feature.notices.a2: In the desktop app, click ⚙ Settings while it shows a number, or open Settings → Overview → What's new. In the terminal app, run coxswain --whats-new.
feature.notices.a3: Not from the app: dismissed tips are kept in the state file. What each led to is still there, such as Settings → Finding files → Details → Meaning, or coxswain --meaning on.
feature.notices.q1: What does the number on the Settings button count?
feature.notices.q2: How do I see what an upgrade brought?
feature.notices.q3: I dismissed a tip by mistake. Can I get it back?
feature.notices.title: Notices and what's new
feature.notices.what: Tips on what you could turn on, and what each upgrade brought: in Settings → Overview, or the status line.
feature.office.a1: No. The quick view needs nothing installed. LibreOffice only adds the exact rendering, and is needed for .ppt, .odp and the other formats without a quick view.
feature.office.a2: The first view is drawn by the app and misses some fonts, effects and charts. LibreOffice's exact rendering then takes its place and is cached for next time.
feature.office.a3: No. Coxswain runs LibreOffice with a profile of its own in the cache folder, so a running LibreOffice neither takes over the conversion nor sees it.
feature.office.q1: Do I need LibreOffice to see a PowerPoint deck?
feature.office.q2: Why do the slides look slightly different, then change?
feature.office.q3: Does it disturb a LibreOffice I have open?
feature.office.title: PowerPoint and Office
feature.office.what: Shows PowerPoint decks at once, then LibreOffice's exact view; other Office files as LibreOffice's PDF.
feature.opening_files.a1: The opener (xdg-open or open) found no application for that type. Set a default application in your system settings, or open the file with {edit} or a user-menu entry.
feature.opening_files.a2: There is no Open with menu. Add a user-menu entry for that application, such as gimp %s, or type it on the command line with {copy_path} to add the name.
feature.opening_files.a3: {open} hands it to the desktop, which may open it in an editor. Run it from the command line (./build.sh), or put it in the scripts folder so {user_menu} runs it. The terminal app runs programs itself.
feature.opening_files.q1: Enter on a file does nothing, and there is no error.
feature.opening_files.q2: How do I open a file with another application than the default?
feature.opening_files.q3: How do I run a script from the desktop app?
feature.opening_files.title: Opening files
feature.opening_files.what: {open} or a double-click goes into a folder or archive, and opens a file in its default application.
feature.own_theme.a1: Your own table of that name replaces the built-in theme, and every slot you did not set takes NC's colours. Copy the whole theme from coxswain --dump-config, or give yours a new name.
feature.own_theme.a2: It has no look, so it gets NC's dos look. Add look = "modern" (or any other look) to its table.
feature.own_theme.a3: The desktop app reads config.toml when it starts and with every change made in Settings. Check the table is [themes.<name>], plural, and that the file still parses.
feature.own_theme.q1: I set [themes.cyber.panel] to tweak Cyber, and everything else turned blue.
feature.own_theme.q2: Why is my theme square and monospaced?
feature.own_theme.q3: My theme is not in the list in Settings.
feature.own_theme.title: Your own theme
feature.own_theme.what: A table in config.toml that sets the colours of up to 31 slots and, for the desktop app, a look.
feature.pack_and_extract.a1: No: Coxswain always makes one, so loose files never spill into a folder. Open the archive with {open} instead, mark everything and copy it with {copy}.
feature.pack_and_extract.a2: Yes. In the desktop app choose tar.gz in the Format list; in the terminal app press Tab in the target prompt until the name ends in .tar.gz. Typing the ending works in both.
feature.pack_and_extract.a3: A folder of the archive's name is already in the target. Rename or remove it, or extract into another folder.
feature.pack_and_extract.q1: Can I extract without the extra folder?
feature.pack_and_extract.title: Pack and extract
feature.pack_and_extract.what: {pack} packs the marked files into a new zip, 7z or tar; {extract} unpacks an archive into a new folder named after it.
feature.preview_data.a1: It does not parse, or it is over 512 KB and was cut off. The source is shown instead; fix the error or open it with {edit}.
feature.preview_data.a2: Yes. SQLite files are opened read-only, and counting rows stops after about a second per table (the count then shows –).
feature.preview_data.a3: It expires within 30 days. Red means it has expired. A .pem with a chain shows every certificate in it, the server's first.
feature.preview_data.q1: My JSON file shows as text, not as a tree.
feature.preview_data.q2: Is it safe to preview a database another program is writing to?
feature.preview_data.q3: Why is a certificate shown in yellow?
feature.preview_data.title: Data files
feature.preview_data.what: Shows JSON, YAML and TOML as trees, CSV and workbooks as tables, databases as tables, certificates as facts.
feature.preview_diagrams.a1: No. All three are drawn by code that ships with Coxswain. Only PlantUML needs plantuml installed or a container.
feature.preview_diagrams.a2: The shapes of draw.io's extra libraries (AWS, Azure, Cisco) come from the web, and the preview never fetches anything. Open the file in draw.io for the real icons.
feature.preview_diagrams.a3: plantuml is not installed and the container image is not pulled yet. A pull never starts by itself: click Render once, or Pull the image in Settings → Previews.
feature.preview_diagrams.q1: Do I need draw.io, Graphviz or Mermaid installed?
feature.preview_diagrams.q2: Why do some draw.io shapes show as plain boxes?
feature.preview_diagrams.q3: PlantUML never draws; the button says Render.
feature.preview_diagrams.title: Diagrams
feature.preview_diagrams.what: Draws draw.io, Mermaid, Graphviz and PlantUML files in the preview pane instead of showing their source.
feature.preview_documents.a1: The pane is for a quick look: it skips the cover and title pages and shows the first chapter with real text. Press {open} to read it in your e-book reader.
feature.preview_documents.a2: The older .doc format needs LibreOffice. Install it, so soffice is found, or set a LibreOffice container image under Previews.
feature.preview_documents.a3: Files over 25 MB are not rendered as documents, as reading them would hold up the pane. Press {open} to open it in its program.
feature.preview_documents.q1: Why does the EPUB show only the first chapter?
feature.preview_documents.q2: Why is a .doc (not .docx) file not shown?
feature.preview_documents.q3: A Word document or notebook says "Too large to preview".
feature.preview_documents.title: Documents
feature.preview_documents.what: Shows PDFs, Word files, e-books, notebooks, e-mails, AsciiDoc, calendars and contacts in the preview pane.
feature.preview_media.a1: The webview lacks the codec. On Linux, install the GStreamer plugins for it (gst-plugins-good, gst-plugins-bad, gst-libav), or press {open} to play it in your media player.
feature.preview_media.a2: Coxswain copies that one file out into its cache folder and previews the copy; the next look replaces it. Files over 256 MB are not copied just for a look.
feature.preview_media.a3: They are the photo's own EXIF data, read on your machine. Nothing is sent; copy the numbers into a map yourself.
feature.preview_media.q1: Why does a video not play?
feature.preview_media.q2: How is a file inside an archive previewed?
feature.preview_media.q3: Where do the GPS numbers come from, and are they sent anywhere?
feature.preview_media.title: Media and files
feature.preview_media.what: Shows pictures with their EXIF facts, plays video and audio, draws fonts, lists archives and sums up folders.
feature.preview_safety.a1: A preview never runs a file's scripts, writes next to files, or lets a repository make git run its programs. Only {open} hands a file to its program.
feature.preview_safety.a2: Files use web pictures to report that they were opened, so the webview loads only the app and your disk. Press {open} for a program that fetches them.
feature.preview_safety.a3: Only in the cache folder: tool results and LibreOffice's profile. Settings → Previews → Previews made so far → Clear removes the results.
feature.preview_safety.q1: Can opening a folder of downloads in Coxswain harm my machine?
feature.preview_safety.q2: Why are pictures from the web missing in a Markdown preview?
feature.preview_safety.q3: Does a preview leave anything behind?
feature.preview_safety.title: Preview safety and limits
feature.preview_safety.what: Previews never run a file's scripts, write next to it or reach the web, and large files are shown in part.
feature.preview_tools.a1: The tool waits for a click (LaTeX with automatic builds off), or the only engine is a container whose image is not pulled yet. The note under the button says which.
feature.preview_tools.a2: No. It shows the line for your system with Copy and never runs it. Paste it into a terminal, or click Settings → Previews to use a container instead.
feature.preview_tools.a3: Coxswain looks on the PATH the app was started with. A session started before the install may have the old PATH: start Coxswain again.
feature.preview_tools.q1: Why does the preview show a button instead of rendering?
feature.preview_tools.q2: The preview says to install a program. Does Coxswain install it?
feature.preview_tools.q3: I installed a program, but the button still says it is not installed.
feature.preview_tools.title: Previews made by tools
feature.preview_tools.what: Makes previews with an installed program or a container: LaTeX, LibreOffice, PlantUML, pandoc, DuckDB.
feature.privacy.a1: Only what the page lists. With update checks off and search by meaning off or on the built-in model (after its one download), nothing does.
feature.privacy.a2: No. The cache and state folders are readable by you alone, and the search helper answers only to a connection with its token, kept in a file only you can read.
feature.privacy.a3: Only what any web request sends: your IP address to GitHub, and the app's User-Agent. No machine ID, no file names, no settings.
feature.privacy.q2: Can other users on the same machine see my index?
feature.privacy.q3: Does the update check send anything about me?
feature.privacy.title: Privacy
feature.privacy.what: No telemetry and no account: what Coxswain learns stays on your disk, and every network request is listed.
feature.properties.a1: No, only the permission bits (or the read-only flag on Windows). Changing the owner needs administrator rights; use sudo chown on the command line.
feature.properties.a2: No, only the folder itself. For everything inside, use chmod -R on the command line.
feature.properties.a3: Its window only shows the facts. Use the command line (chmod 755 deploy.sh); your file flags are changed with {menu} → File flags.
feature.properties.q2: Does changing a folder's permissions change the files in it?
feature.properties.q3: How do I change permissions in the terminal app?
feature.properties.title: Properties and permissions
feature.properties.what: {properties} shows a file's size, dates, owner, permissions, ZFS dataset, package and flags; the desktop app can change them.
feature.provenance.a1: No. It means a file here has the digest the provenance names. Coxswain does not verify the signature, so the view says Not verified; use slsa-verifier or gh attestation verify.
feature.provenance.a2: Coxswain never fetches. Run git fetch in your checkout and move off the provenance and back on, or open the other pane in your checkout.
feature.provenance.a3: It is looked for by the name the provenance gives, in its folder and the other pane's. A file renamed after the build is not found.
feature.provenance.q1: Does a ✓ mean the file is safe?
feature.provenance.q2: Why is my commit "not in your checkout"?
feature.provenance.q3: Why does an output say "not here" when the file is right there?
feature.provenance.title: Build provenance
feature.provenance.what: Shows a provenance file as inputs, build and outputs, and checks outputs and commit against your disk.
feature.quick_search.a1: Those keys are bound to an action, such as Colour tag or Git branches, and a bound key does its action. Start with another letter of the name, or unbind the action.
feature.quick_search.a2: No, only the start of names. Open Find ({search}), press it again for In <folder>, and Tab once for Names: that searches names in this folder and below.
feature.quick_search.a3: The terminal keeps Alt for itself, or on a Mac turns Option+letter into a special character. Turn on Use Option as Meta key (Terminal) or set Option to Esc+ (iTerm2).
feature.quick_search.q1: Why do some Alt+letters not start a quick search?
feature.quick_search.q2: Can it find letters in the middle of a name?
feature.quick_search.q3: Alt+letter does nothing in my terminal. Why?
feature.quick_search.title: Quick search
feature.quick_search.what: Hold Alt and type how a name starts: the cursor jumps to the first entry in the panel that fits.
feature.removable_disks.a1: The disk is not plugged in or not mounted. Its text is kept out of sight and comes back when it is mounted again, wherever. Settings shows it as away.
feature.removable_disks.a2: At the helper's next pass over the folders, within ten minutes. Read now in Settings starts one at once.
feature.removable_disks.a3: Press Remove next to it under Settings → Finding files → Details → Folders → Folders read.
feature.removable_disks.q1: Why did my disk's files disappear from search?
feature.removable_disks.q2: I plugged the disk back in. When do its files come back?
feature.removable_disks.q3: How do I get rid of an old disk's text?
feature.removable_disks.title: Removable disks
feature.removable_disks.what: A folder on a USB stick or external drive can be read; its text is kept while unplugged and found again anywhere.
feature.scans.a1: The notice ends with the command for your system. In the desktop app click Copy next to it in Settings → Overview; in the terminal app press Space on tesseract under Programs that read more. Run it in a shell.
feature.scans.a2: The helper looks for the programs when it starts. Make any change under Settings → Finding files, or close every Coxswain window and wait ten minutes. The ✓ in Settings shows it was found.
feature.scans.a3: A JPEG whose EXIF names a camera maker is a photo, and photos are skipped on purpose: they seldom have words and there are thousands.
feature.scans.q1: A notice says to install tesseract. How?
feature.scans.q2: I installed tesseract and nothing happened.
feature.scans.q3: Why are my holiday photos not read?
feature.scans.title: Scans and older Office files
feature.scans.what: With tesseract, pdftoppm or LibreOffice installed, finds words in pictures, scanned PDFs and old Office files.
feature.scripts.a1: Settings → Keys names it on the line {user_menu} scripts folder, and Open the folder opens it in the active pane, made first when it is not there.
feature.scripts.a2: Look at the status line: the error is there. Usually the script is not executable (chmod +x), or its first line is not a #! line.
feature.scripts.a3: No, script files have no key. Add a user-menu entry that runs the script and give that entry a key. The terminal app has no scripts; a user-menu entry works there too.
feature.scripts.q2: My script is in the menu but nothing happens.
feature.scripts.q3: Can I give a script a key?
feature.scripts.title: Scripts
feature.scripts.what: Programs in the scripts folder next to your config are entries of the desktop app's {user_menu} menu, run on the marked files.
feature.search_archives.a1: Yes, when the zip is in a folder that is read (your home folder by default, not a hidden folder or a cache): by name and by words. A zip elsewhere is found by its own name only.
feature.search_archives.a2: Within a second or two by name, and a few seconds later by its text, whoever changed the zip. Without the file watcher, at the next hourly rebuild or within ten minutes.
feature.search_archives.a3: They are programs' archives and would fill the results, so caches are left out. Tick Archives everywhere in Settings → Finding files → Details → What is read to find their entries by name.
feature.search_archives.q1: Does Find look inside my zip files?
feature.search_archives.q2: I added a file to a zip. When can I find it?
feature.search_archives.q3: Why are the archives in ~/.m2 or ~/.cache not looked into?
feature.search_archives.title: Search inside archives
feature.search_archives.what: Files inside zip, 7z and tar archives are found by name, words, meaning and Ask; Enter opens them in the archive.
feature.search_diagrams.a1: The arrow from Browser to Entra ID became the sentence "Browser to Entra ID: …", which has both words.
feature.search_diagrams.a2: Yes, a fenced block that starts with ```mermaid or ~~~mermaid. An arrow written in the Markdown text outside such a block is not read as one.
feature.search_diagrams.a3: Its line has a form the patterns do not know, or in draw.io one of its ends is not a shape with a label. Its words are still in the text.
feature.search_diagrams.q1: Why does browser entra find my diagram, when no box says both?
feature.search_diagrams.q2: Does a Mermaid block in my README count?
feature.search_diagrams.q3: Why is one arrow missing from the sentences?
feature.search_diagrams.title: Diagrams read as sentences
feature.search_diagrams.what: Each arrow in draw.io, Mermaid, Graphviz and PlantUML diagrams becomes a sentence that words and meaning find.
feature.search_documents.a1: Check it is .docx or .odt, not the older .doc, which needs LibreOffice. It must also be under 20 MB, not locked with a password, and in a folder read.
feature.search_documents.a2: No, the values the cells show. A formula's result is found; the formula is not.
feature.search_documents.a3: Their names are, so budget.xlsx finds the mail that had it attached. Their contents are not.
feature.search_documents.q1: Why is a Word document not found by its text?
feature.search_documents.q2: Does it find the formulas in my spreadsheet?
feature.search_documents.q3: Are the attachments of a mail read?
feature.search_documents.title: Documents it reads
feature.search_documents.what: Reads PDFs, Word, OpenDocument, spreadsheets, slides, mail, books and notebooks itself, so their words are found.
feature.search_folders.a1: In the desktop app, add it under Settings → Finding files → Details → Folders → Names only. From any app, put an empty file named .nosearch in it.
feature.search_folders.a2: Listing folders replaces the default. Add your home folder to Folders read too.
feature.search_folders.a3: The helper reads the config when it starts. Make any change under Settings → Finding files, or close every Coxswain window and wait ten minutes.
feature.search_folders.q1: How do I make a folder names-only?
feature.search_folders.q2: I added a folder outside my home folder, and now my home folder is not read.
feature.search_folders.q3: I changed [search] in config.toml by hand and nothing happened.
feature.search_folders.title: Choosing the folders
feature.search_folders.what: Choose which folders have their text read and which are found by name only, with lists or a .nosearch file.
feature.search_history.a1: Repositories are read at the helper's scans, at most ten minutes apart, so wait a little. Commits in a repository outside the folders read are never kept.
feature.search_history.a2: No: the messages, authors and changed paths. Files are searched as they are on disk. To read a file as it was, open the commit and preview it.
feature.search_history.a3: Put an empty .nosearch file in the repository, or add it to Names only: then neither its files nor its commits are read.
feature.search_history.q1: Why does Find miss my latest commit?
feature.search_history.q2: Does it search the code as it was in old commits?
feature.search_history.q3: Can I keep one repository's history out?
feature.search_history.title: Git history in search
feature.search_history.what: Find searches the commit messages, authors and changed paths of your git repositories, under History.
feature.search_settings.a1: It needs a model that is not there yet: the built-in model or a server for meaning, a chat model for Ask. The guide finds the servers on this machine and says what suits it.
feature.search_settings.a2: Nothing waits to be read, or the helper cannot be reached; the Words line then says Not running, with Start it.
feature.search_settings.a3: No. The search settings are for the machine: one helper serves every window. Per folder there are Names only and a .nosearch file.
feature.search_settings.q1: Why does a level open the setup guide instead of turning on?
feature.search_settings.q2: Why is Read now greyed out?
feature.search_settings.q3: Can I set these per folder or per window?
feature.search_settings.title: Search settings
feature.search_settings.what: Settings → Finding files: how each part of search stands, four levels of how far Find looks, and every switch.
feature.search_setup.a1: Yes. Leave The built-in model chosen in step 2 and press Download the built-in model in step 3. Ask works without a server too, with the built-in chat model in step 4.
feature.search_setup.a2: In the desktop app, press {settings} and Set up… in Overview or Finding files, or the set it up link in Find. In the terminal app, run coxswain --setup-search.
feature.search_setup.a3: It asks localhost on the usual ports only. An Ollama on another port, or in a container without the port published, is not found: type its address under A server on another machine.
feature.search_setup.q1: I have no Ollama or any server. Does search by meaning work?
feature.search_setup.q2: How do I start the guide?
feature.search_setup.q3: The guide finds no server, but Ollama is running. Why?
feature.search_setup.title: Smart search setup
feature.search_setup.what: A guided setup for text, meaning and Ask: finds model servers, suits your hardware, asks before downloading.
feature.servers.a1: A multilingual embedding model if your files are in several languages: bge-m3 is the suggestion. Any embedding model the server offers works; chat models do not.
feature.servers.a2: Vectors of two models cannot be compared, so every file gets new ones. You are asked first, with the number of files and about how long. bge-m3 and bge-m3:latest count as the same model.
feature.servers.a3: In an environment variable, named under API key from the environment variable. It must be set where the search helper starts; the key goes only to the saved server.
feature.servers.q1: Which model should I pick on a server?
feature.servers.q2: Why does switching the model start over?
feature.servers.q3: My server wants an API key. Where does it go?
feature.servers.title: Meaning on a model server
feature.servers.what: Ollama, Lemonade, LM Studio or another OpenAI-style server makes the vectors for search by meaning, on its GPU.
feature.session.a1: Quit it, then delete state.json or just its session part. Deleting the whole file also drops favourites, tags and notes.
feature.session.a2: No. Start it in that folder, or name it: coxswain ~/projects/rocket.
feature.session.a3: It is moved aside to state.json.bad and the app starts with defaults, so nothing is overwritten.
feature.session.q1: How do I reset the desktop app's layout?
feature.session.q2: Does the terminal app remember the last folder?
feature.session.title: What the apps remember
feature.session.what: The desktop app comes back with its tabs, folders, views and widths; the terminal app starts fresh.
feature.settings_window.a1: No. It edits the one value in place and keeps every comment, blank line and other key. If the file does not exist yet, it is created with only what you changed.
feature.settings_window.a2: No. Language, theme, fonts and sizes apply at once, and search changes restart the search helper. Changes made to config.toml by hand need a restart.
feature.settings_window.a3: Most terminals do not pass Ctrl+, on. Use {menu} → Settings, the gear button in the desktop app, or coxswain --settings; or give the action another key.
feature.settings_window.q1: Will Settings mess up my hand-written config?
feature.settings_window.q2: Do I have to restart the desktop app after a change in Settings?
feature.settings_window.q3: Where is the Settings key if {settings} does nothing?
feature.settings_window.title: Settings
feature.settings_window.what: {settings} opens Settings: every option in plain words, saved to config.toml at once with your comments kept.
feature.sidebar.a1: Drives is read again every 30 seconds and when you come back to the window, so it shows within half a minute. If not, it is mounted somewhere left out with the system mounts.
feature.sidebar.a2: A place is listed only when your system names it and it exists; on Linux the names come from ~/.config/user-dirs.dirs. Add the folder to a favourites group instead.
feature.sidebar.a3: You hid it with {toggle_sidebar}, and that is remembered. Press it again.
feature.sidebar.q1: Why is my USB stick not in the sidebar?
feature.sidebar.q2: Why is my Desktop (or Music, or Videos) not under Places?
feature.sidebar.q3: Why is the sidebar gone after a restart?
feature.sidebar.title: The sidebar
feature.sidebar.what: Places, drives with their free space, favourites and recent git repositories, in the desktop app.
feature.sorting.a1: Press {sort_time}. Press it again for the oldest first.
feature.sorting.a2: The order uses the sizes the file system gives, and a folder's is not its contents. Folder sizes are shown, but folders stay in name order among themselves.
feature.sorting.a3: The desktop app remembers the switch in its session, and that wins over the setting. Press {toggle_hidden} once to show them again.
feature.sorting.q1: How do I see the newest files first?
feature.sorting.q2: Why are folders not sorted by their size?
feature.sorting.q3: Hidden files stay hidden after a restart of the desktop app. Why?
feature.sorting.title: Sorting and hidden files
feature.sorting.what: Sort a panel by name, extension, time or size, and show or hide hidden files.
feature.tabs_and_panes.a1: Not planned. Two panels with one folder each is its layout; for more places at once, run it in several terminal tabs.
feature.tabs_and_panes.a2: To the folder of the pane you see: the dialog offers it, and you can type another one. With two panes they offer the other pane's folder.
feature.tabs_and_panes.a3: It shows what the terminal had before the panels: the output of commands run from the command line, or nothing when none ran yet. Press any key to return.
feature.tabs_and_panes.q1: Are tabs coming to the terminal app?
feature.tabs_and_panes.q2: Where do {copy} and {move} copy to with one pane?
feature.tabs_and_panes.q3: Why does {toggle_panels} in the terminal app show an empty screen?
feature.tabs_and_panes.title: Tabs and panes
feature.tabs_and_panes.what: Tabs with their own folder, view and history in the desktop app; back and forward; one pane or two.
feature.tags.a1: A tag belongs to a path, not to the file. Renaming or moving leaves it at the old path; tag the file again under its new name.
feature.tags.a2: Yes. Mark them, then press {tag} and a digit. Every marked file gets that colour; 0 removes the tag from all of them.
feature.tags.a3: No. The terminal app has no tags, and {tag} there says Colour tag is available in the desktop app. The tags stay for the desktop app.
feature.tags.q1: Why is a tag gone after I renamed a file?
feature.tags.q2: Can I tag many files at once?
feature.tags.q3: Does the terminal app show tags I set in the desktop app?
feature.tags.title: Colour tags
feature.tags.what: A coloured dot after a file's or folder's name, in one of seven colours, in the desktop app.
feature.terminal_app.a1: There is no preview pane in the terminal. {view} opens it in your viewer (viewer, else $PAGER, else less); quit the viewer to come back.
feature.terminal_app.a2: Press {menu}, type set, Enter. Settings opens full screen; Space flips a switch and the bottom line says Saved to …/config.toml.
feature.terminal_app.a3: Both apps share one keymap, so your keys work the same in each. The terminal app names desktop-only actions in the status line instead of doing nothing.
feature.terminal_app.q1: How do I see a file's contents without leaving the panels?
feature.terminal_app.q2: How do I change a setting without editing config.toml?
feature.terminal_app.q3: A key said "is available in the desktop app". Why is it there at all?
feature.terminal_app.title: The terminal app
feature.terminal_app.what: Coxswain in a terminal: two Norton Commander panels that work in any terminal and over SSH.
feature.text.a1: It is read within seconds if it is in a folder read, not left out, under 20 MB, and the machine is not on battery. A backlog shows as still to read in Find's footer.
feature.text.a2: Only the last word may be the start of a word; the others must be whole words. Put the partial word last, or type it in full.
feature.text.a3: Settings → Finding files → Details → Background reading → Delete what was read, then click again. Or delete search.db while no Coxswain runs.
feature.text.q1: Why doesn't a file I just saved show up?
feature.text.q2: Why does budge not find budgets?
feature.text.q3: How do I start the index afresh?
feature.text.title: Text in files
feature.text.what: Finds files by the words inside them: code, notes, PDFs, Office files, mail and books, read in the background.
feature.text_and_code.a1: When the command line has text, Space belongs to it. Press Esc to clear the line, or use {view}, which always toggles the pane.
feature.text_and_code.a2: Files over 200 KB stay plain so scrolling stays smooth; over 512 KB only the first 512 KB is read. Press {edit} to see all of it in your editor.
feature.text_and_code.a3: Git has no earlier version of an untracked file to compare against. Once you git add it, Diff appears and shows the whole file as added.
feature.text_and_code.q1: Space types a space in the command line instead of opening the preview.
feature.text_and_code.q2: Why is a large file shown without colours?
feature.text_and_code.q3: Why is there no Diff button on a new file?
feature.text_and_code.title: Text and code
feature.text_and_code.what: Shows code, logs and text highlighted in the theme's colours, Markdown rendered, and a changed file's diff.
feature.the_screen.a1: In the desktop app, the pane with the coloured frame; in the terminal app, the one whose path is in the cursor colour and shows the cursor bar. {switch_panel} or a click switches.
feature.the_screen.a2: The panel is narrower than 44 columns inside its border, so only Name and Size fit. Make the terminal wider.
feature.the_screen.a3: The folder it was started in is not open in any left-pane tab, so it is added. Keep a tab on that folder (home, when started from the desktop menu) and none is added.
feature.the_screen.q2: Why is the Modified column gone in the terminal app?
feature.the_screen.q3: Why is there a new tab in the left pane every time I start the desktop app?
feature.the_screen.title: The screen
feature.the_screen.what: Two panels, a command line and a row of function keys, as in Norton Commander; the active panel is lit.
feature.themes.a1: A terminal draws characters in cells, so the terminal app takes a theme's colours only. Bevels, title bars, corners and fonts are the desktop app's looks.
feature.themes.a2: The built-in themes use exact #rrggbb colours and need a terminal with true colour. In tmux, enable it; over ssh, check that COLORTERM=truecolor reaches the other side.
feature.themes.a3: Yes: give both keys the same name, theme at the top of config.toml and theme under [gui]. They stay separate so each app can have its own.
feature.themes.q1: Why does the terminal app not have the Windows 95 bevels?
feature.themes.q2: The colours in my terminal look washed out, or wrong.
feature.themes.q3: Can the two apps use the same theme?
feature.themes.title: Themes
feature.themes.what: Eighteen built-in colour sets, from Cyber and Norton Commander blue to Windows 3.11–11 and Mac; each app has its own.
feature.undo.a1: A move to the bin, yes, except on a Mac and in the Flatpak, where you restore it from the system's bin. Deleting for good ({delete_forever}) cannot be undone.
feature.undo.a2: Some programs write when they open or save. Undo compares the size and modification time to what the operation left, and leaves a changed file alone.
feature.undo.a3: No. The history lives in memory, for the app run. After a restart, a move to the bin can still be restored from the system's bin.
feature.undo.q2: Undo said changed since. I only opened the file.
feature.undo.q3: Can I undo after restarting Coxswain?
feature.undo.title: Undo
feature.undo.what: {undo} undoes the last file operation (copy, move, rename, new folder, move to the bin, pack, extract), up to 20 back.
feature.updates.a1: No. It only tells you. Updating is left to the way you installed it, so your package manager stays in charge.
feature.updates.a2: The running app is the old one: quit every Coxswain window and the terminal app, then start again. coxswain --version shows the version you now have.
feature.updates.a3: Update. Or untick Check for a new version in Settings → Privacy and updates; the button goes at the next hourly look or when the app starts again.
feature.updates.q2: I updated, but it still says a newer version is available.
feature.updates.q3: How do I get rid of the update button?
feature.updates.title: Update checks
feature.updates.what: Once a day, asks GitHub whether a newer release exists and names the command that upgrades your copy.
feature.user_menu.a1: Your own list replaces the built-in one. Press {user_menu}, then +: on a config without entries, the built-in ones are written in, commented out. Take the # off those you want.
feature.user_menu.a2: It is left out when no terminal is found or there is no desktop (a text console, ssh), and in Termux. Set $TERMINAL to yours, or add your own entry.
feature.user_menu.a3: No. Coxswain already quotes each name when it needs it; your own quotes would end up as part of the name.
feature.user_menu.q1: My entries replaced the built-in ones. How do I keep both?
feature.user_menu.q2: Why is Open a terminal here not in my menu?
feature.user_menu.title: User menu
feature.user_menu.what: A menu of shell commands, each with a key of its own, that can work on the file under the cursor or the marked files.
feature.view_and_edit.a1: The desktop app starts the editor without a terminal, so hx, vim or nano have nowhere to show. Set editor to a windowed editor, or leave it out so files open in their default application.
feature.view_and_edit.a2: The first that is set: editor in config.toml, then $VISUAL, then $EDITOR, then vi (notepad on Windows). For {view}: viewer, then $PAGER, then less.
feature.view_and_edit.a3: No: the editor would change a copy, and the change would be lost. Copy it out with {copy} first.
feature.view_and_edit.q1: {edit} in the desktop app does nothing, though a terminal editor works in the terminal app.
feature.view_and_edit.q2: Which editor does the terminal app pick?
feature.view_and_edit.q3: Can I edit a file inside an archive?
feature.view_and_edit.title: View and edit
feature.view_and_edit.what: {view} views the file under the cursor and {edit} edits it; in the desktop app {view} is the preview pane.
feature.views.a1: That is the details view, as in Norton Commander. In the columns view ({toggle_view} once) Left goes out and Right goes in; {parent} goes up in every view.
feature.views.a2: The pane is narrower than about 620 pixels. Widen it, hide the sidebar ({toggle_sidebar}) or switch to one pane ({toggle_panels}).
feature.views.a3: Thumbnails are the pictures themselves, decoded at full size; there is no thumbnail cache. Tiles load as they scroll into sight.
feature.views.q1: Why does Left jump a page instead of going to the parent folder?
feature.views.q2: Why did Type and Modified's date disappear?
feature.views.q3: Why is my photo folder slow in thumbnails?
feature.views.title: Details, columns and thumbnails
feature.views.what: Show a folder as details, Miller columns or thumbnails, chosen per tab, in the desktop app.
feature.where_things_are_kept.a1: Usually search.db (the text of your files) and models/ (488 MB with the built-in model), then previews/. Settings shows the size of each.
