feature.where_things_are_kept.a2: Copy state.json while no Coxswain runs. Tags and notes are kept by full path, so they show only where the same paths exist.
feature.where_things_are_kept.a3: A state.json that could not be read at start, moved aside so a new one could be saved. Your tags and notes are in it; mend it by hand or delete it.
feature.where_things_are_kept.q1: The cache folder is large. What takes the room?
feature.where_things_are_kept.q2: How do I copy my tags, notes and favourites to another machine?
feature.where_things_are_kept.title: Where things are kept
feature.where_things_are_kept.what: Lists where settings, state and caches live on each system; coxswain --paths prints them for your machine.
feature.windows_arm.a1: Coxswain_<version>_arm64-setup.exe. The x64 installer works too, under emulation, but slower.
feature.windows_arm.a2: In Task Manager's Details tab, the Architecture column shows ARM64 for coxswain-gui.exe or coxswain.exe. Right-click the headings to add the column.
feature.windows_arm.a3: The built-in model does not; it runs on the processor. A model server that uses the NPU or GPU can do the work instead.
feature.windows_arm.q1: Which installer do I need on a Snapdragon laptop?
feature.windows_arm.q2: How do I know whether I am running the ARM build?
feature.windows_arm.q3: Does search by meaning use the NPU?
feature.windows_arm.title: Windows on ARM
feature.windows_arm.what: Native arm64 builds of both apps for Windows on ARM, such as Snapdragon X laptops, run without x64 emulation.
feature.zfs_snapshots.a1: Press {snapshots} in the folder it was in, Enter on a snapshot from before, then {copy} on the file to copy it to the other panel. Copying never overwrites.
feature.zfs_snapshots.a2: No. Listing snapshots and reading .zfs/snapshot work for every user. You see the files the permissions let you see.
feature.zfs_snapshots.a3: No, on purpose: Coxswain only reads. Use zfs snapshot and zfs destroy, from the command line or a user-menu entry.
feature.zfs_snapshots.q1: How do I get back a file I deleted, or an older version of it?
feature.zfs_snapshots.q2: Do I need root, or zfs allow?
feature.zfs_snapshots.q3: Can I take or destroy snapshots from Coxswain?
feature.zfs_snapshots.title: ZFS snapshots as folders
feature.zfs_snapshots.what: {snapshots} lists a ZFS dataset's snapshots; open one to browse the folder as it was and copy old files back.

setting.mono_font.hint: For file contents, paths and code.
setting.name_exclude.hint: Paths (/proc) and folder names (.cache) the name index skips: not found even by name.
setting.name_roots.hint: The folders the name index covers. None: the whole machine.
setting.names_only.hint: Found by name and counted in folder sizes, but never opened. An empty file named .nosearch in a folder does the same.
setting.preview_container.hint: The program that runs containers. No containers: only installed programs make previews.
setting.preview_prefer.hint: For LaTeX, PlantUML, Word and the like: an installed program is quickest; a container needs nothing but podman or docker.
setting.preview_timeout.hint: How long a tool may take for one preview before it is stopped.
setting.provenance_viewer.hint: F3 on build provenance (SLSA, in-toto, a Sigstore bundle) opens the provenance viewer; F3 again shows the source. Off: it opens in the viewer like any file.
setting.right_click.hint: What a right-click on a file or folder does. Ctrl+right-click in the desktop app does the other.
setting.search_archives.hint: Zip, 7z and tar: the files in them are found by name and by their text.
setting.search_archives_everywhere.hint: Also archives in caches and programs' folders, by name: a larger name index that takes longer to build.
setting.search_cloud: Read files that are only online
setting.search_cloud.hint: OneDrive, Dropbox, Google Drive, Proton Drive, iCloud: files kept only online are found by name and never downloaded, unless this is on. On, reading one downloads it.
setting.search_history.hint: Commit messages, authors and changed paths of the git repositories in the folders read.
setting.search_meaning.hint: Finds files about your words, not only files with them, in any language: “rocket fuel cost” finds a Danish budget.
setting.search_text.hint: Reads the text of your files in the background and keeps it on this machine, so Find finds files by the words in them.
setting.show_hidden: Show hidden files when Coxswain starts
setting.show_hidden.hint: Names starting with a dot, and files marked hidden. Alt+. shows or hides them at any time.
setting.text_exclude.hint: Folder names (node_modules) and file patterns (*.log, secret*) never read, wherever they are. They are still found by name.
setting.text_max_size.hint: Larger files are found by name only.
setting.text_roots.hint: Their files are found by name and by the words in them. None: your home folder.
setting.theme.hint: Its colours, and with some themes their own font and shapes.
setting.tui_theme.hint: The terminal app's colours, from the same list of themes. It takes the new one when it starts again.
setting.viewer.hint: The program F3 shows a file in. Empty: $PAGER, else less.
setting.watch.hint: New, renamed and deleted files show in Find at once. Off: the names are gathered again once an hour.
settings.ask_builtin_hint: A built-in model answers without a server. It is loaded for the first question and let go after five minutes without one, which frees its memory.

settings.keys_hint: Keys are changed in config.toml under [keys]; both apps read them when they start.
settings.language_improve: Translations marked new are fresh: if a word reads wrong or clumsy, help improve it.
settings.level.ask.hint: Also questions, answered from your files by a chat model.

settings.level.meaning.hint: Also files about your words, in any language.

settings.level.text.hint: Also the words inside your files.

setup.ask_builtin: {model}, built in ({size} download, {where}; nothing leaves the machine)
setup.ask_builtin_hint: Optional. A built-in chat model answers on this machine, with nothing to install, and nothing leaves it: quickly on a Mac's GPU, slowly on a processor alone (a minute or more before the first word). A model server answers more quickly with larger models.
setup.ask_hint: Only models that can answer are listed. For this machine: {model}. A test question shows how quickly it answers.
setup.builtin: The built-in model ({size} download, {where}; nothing leaves the machine)
setup.builtin_hint: multilingual-e5-small: 100 languages, runs on any machine. Every file is read again when you switch to it.
setup.builtin_on: Search by meaning is on, with the built-in model. The search helper now reads your files for meaning in the background; hits by meaning show up in searches as it goes.
setup.cpu_lemonade: Lemonade runs {model} on the processor, but this machine has {gpu}. In Lemonade's model manager, choose a Hybrid or NPU model, or a GGUF model with the Vulkan or ROCm backend.
setup.cpu_lmstudio: LM Studio does not say where it runs a model. To use {gpu}, set GPU offload to the maximum in the model's settings in LM Studio.
setup.cpu_ollama: Ollama runs {model} on the processor, but this machine has {gpu}. How to make Ollama use it: {url}
setup.cpu_ollama_arch: Ollama runs {model} on the processor, but this machine has {gpu}. Install Ollama's GPU build: sudo pacman -S {package}, then restart Ollama (systemctl restart ollama).
setup.embed_hint: Only models that make vectors are listed. {model} is a good choice: it knows many languages and is small.
setup.found: {server} at {url}: {embed} models for vectors, {chat} for answers
setup.intro: Four kinds of search work together: names (always on), words inside files, meaning (what a file is about, in any language) and Ask (a chat model answers from your files and names its sources). Each step below can be skipped, and nothing is downloaded until you say so.
setup.looking: Looking for model servers on this machine…
setup.none_found: No model server answers on this machine. Install one (see the guide) and look again, or use the built-in model.
setup.open_hint: A guide through search inside files, by meaning and Ask: it finds the model servers on this machine and says what suits it.
setup.other_hint: A server on another machine gets your questions and the text of your files. Type its address, for example http://192.168.1.20:11434.
setup.pull_elsewhere: {server} downloads models in its own window: find {model} there, download it, then look again here.
setup.server_hint: For search by meaning, a model turns every passage into a vector: numbers for what it means. The built-in model does it on this machine (on the CPU, or on a Mac's GPU); a model server (Ollama, Lemonade, LM Studio, llama.cpp …) uses the graphics card or NPU and is much quicker.
setup.service_hint: Start with my session: the search helper runs from login, so the store follows your files between launches. It uses a little processor time when files change and pauses on battery. No administrator rights are needed (a systemd user service on Linux, a launchd agent on macOS, a Run entry on Windows, an XDG autostart entry on FreeBSD).
setup.speed_hint: After the test question, this says whether the server runs the model on the graphics card.
setup.speed_no_gpu: No graphics card or NPU found: models run on the processor. Small models answer, slowly.
setup.speed_ok: The server runs the model on the graphics card.
setup.text_hint: Coxswain reads the text of your files in the background and keeps it in a store on this machine. Meaning and Ask build on it.
setup.title: Set up smart search
setup.try_done: It answered: the first word came after {seconds} s.
setup.use_try: Use and ask a test question
setup.why_amd: {gpu}: Lemonade runs models on AMD's NPU and Radeon graphics. Its embedding model makes the vectors and {chat} answers.
setup.why_apple: Apple silicon with {ram} GB of shared memory: Ollama or LM Studio run the models on its GPU. bge-m3 makes the vectors and {chat} answers.
setup.why_apple_builtin: Apple silicon with {ram} GB of shared memory and no model server: the built-in model makes the vectors on its GPU (Metal), with nothing to install, and nothing leaves the machine. Ask can use the built-in chat model on the GPU too, or stay off.
setup.why_cpu: No graphics card found ({ram} GB of memory): the built-in model makes the vectors on the processor. Ask works with the built-in chat model, slowly, or can stay off.
setup.why_nvidia: {gpu} with {vram} GB: Ollama runs the models on it with CUDA. bge-m3 makes the vectors and {chat} answers; both fit in its memory.
